summary:
FireLens is a geospatial data platform designed to improve the consistency and usability of historical wildfire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments.

Different sensors have different spatial resolutions, observation times, and detection characteristics, making long-term comparisons challenging. FireLens addresses this problem through a scientific data pipeline that integrates active fire observations, analyzes sensor differences, evaluates spatial and temporal relationships, and investigates methods for harmonizing historical records.

Our current research prototype processes nearly 8 million satellite observations from July 2024 across five satellite platforms. It includes data quality assessment, coverage analysis, spatial-temporal comparisons, and measurement characterization.

The long-term vision is an interactive global platform that enables users to explore historical fire activity, compare satellite observations, identify trends, and support more consistent wildfire monitoring and research.
details:
Project Overview

FireLens is a scientific geospatial platform designed to investigate and improve the harmonization of historical active fire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS instruments.

How It Works

The project uses a Python-based data engineering pipeline to ingest, validate, and analyze satellite observations from five platforms: Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21.

The current research pipeline includes:

  • Historical data ingestion and provenance tracking.
  • Data quality assessment and temporal coverage analysis.
  • Spatial and temporal comparisons between satellite observations.
  • Within-sensor clustering and measurement characterization.
  • Experiments investigating spatial resolution, observation timing, and Fire Radiative Power (FRP).

The July 2024 dataset contains approximately 7.98 million observations.

Technology Stack

  • Python, NumPy, SciPy, pandas and scientific analysis tools.
  • React, Vite, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS.
  • CesiumJS for geospatial visualization.
  • Firebase planned for application data and real-time functionality.

Innovation and Impact

Different satellite instruments have different spatial resolutions, observation schedules, and detection characteristics. These differences make historical fire comparisons challenging.

FireLens investigates these differences before applying harmonization methods, with the goal of producing more consistent historical fire activity records.

The planned platform will allow users to explore historical fire activity, compare observations across sensors, identify temporal patterns, and support wildfire monitoring and research.

Current Development Status

The scientific data pipeline and initial research experiments are implemented. Historical harmonization, independent scientific validation, predictive modeling, and the complete interactive visualization platform remain under development.
